title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the Teichmüller notes study a 'combinatorial polygon' P_n with n vertices. Its dihedral group D_{P_n} has order 2n and rotation subgroup D^+_{P_n} ≅ Z/n. Attached to P_n are a Riemann sphere Σ_{P_n} (a complex projective line), a set S_{P_n} of n marked points on a real circle in Σ_{P_n}, and a 2-dimensional real vector space V_{P_n} in which the vertices sit as the vertices of a centred regular n-gon.

Odd n (previous page). The map s ↦ Rs from S into P(V_{P_n})(R) is injective. So P(V_{P_n})(C) satisfies the characteristic properties of Σ_{P_n}: it is a projective line containing S on its real circle, and the D_{P_n}-action comes from a linear action on V_{P_n}.

Even n (this page). One passes to the double cover P̃_{2n}, a 2n-gon with a marked n-subpolygon, and sets Σ_{P_n} = P(V_{P̃_{2n}}). The natural map D_{P̃_{2n}} → D_{P_n} has kernel {±1}, the rotation by π. This is the extension called (8).

Grothendieck shows this map does not split. Its restriction to rotations is Z/2n → Z/n. Writing n = 2m, the element of order 4 in Z/2n maps to the element of order 2 in Z/n. This reduces the question to Z/4 → Z/2, which does not split. (Equivalently, Z/2n ≅ Z/2 × Z/n only when n is odd.)

He then identifies (8) as the pullback of 1 → {±1} → SL(V) → PGL(V) = Aut(Σ_{P_n}) → 1 along D_{P_n} → Aut(Σ_{P_n}). He concludes that the D_{P_n}-action on Σ_{P_n} does not lift to a linear action on V. Equivalently, it does not lift to an action on (Σ_{P_n}, O(1)).

Purpose (next page): only after choosing the double cover P̃_{2n} does one get an action of D_{P̃_{2n}} on the principal C*-bundle PΣ = V(O(1))* and on its restriction PΣ* to Σ* = Σ minus the marked points. Grothendieck wants the fundamental groupoid of PΣ* with this action. This is input for the genus-0, n-point part of the Teichmüller tower, i.e. central extensions and symmetries of braid/mapping-class data around the dihedral symmetric configuration.
errors: The identification of (8) with a pullback of SL(V) → PGL(V) is inaccurate if SL means SL_2(C). The preimage of a dihedral group of order 2n in SL_2(C) is the binary dihedral group of order 4n, not D_{2n}. Moreover, a reflection never lifts to an involution in SL_2(C), so even for odd n there is no SL_2 lift. The statement is correct for the real compact form, 1 → {±1} → O(V_R) → O(V_R)/{±1} → 1, where the pullback is indeed D_{2n}.

A gap in the logic: non-splitting of a {±1}-extension does not by itself exclude a lift to GL(V) with other scalar kernels. The correct invariant is the class in H^2(D_n, C*) (the Schur multiplier, Z/2 for n even and 0 for n odd). For n even it is nonzero because D_n contains a Klein four-group acting on P^1 by the Pauli-type involutions, which does not lift to GL_2. So the conclusion (no linear lift and no D_n-linearization of O(1) for n even) is correct, but the stated argument is incomplete.

The phrase 'se prolonge au quotient ... Z/4 → Z/2' should be a restriction to the order-4 subgroup ⟨m⟩ (pullback), not a quotient. As written, the quotient Z/2n/⟨m⟩ is Z/m, not Z/4. The conclusion is unaffected.

ideas.what: Non-splitting of Z/2n → Z/n for n even, hence of D_{2n} → D_n.
ideas.modern_name: Elementary group extension / cyclic extension non-splitting

ideas.what: Obstruction to lifting the dihedral action on P^1 to a linear action, i.e. to a linearization of O(1), for n even; resolved by passing to the double-cover dihedral group D_{2n}.
ideas.modern_name: Linearization obstruction / Schur multiplier H^2(D_n, C*) ≅ Z/2 for n even; projective representations of dihedral groups

ideas.what: Using the principal C*-bundle of O(1) over the punctured sphere Σ*_{P_n}, with the action of D_{P̃_{2n}}, as the object whose fundamental groupoid is studied (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Central C*-extension / tangential-basepoint-type data for π_1 of M_{0,n}-type configurations; dihedral symmetry in the genus-0 Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Teichmüller tower) in spirit; later Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Schneps for dihedral/genus-0 symmetries
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and symmetric spheres but not this specific construction (unsure).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification of a standard group-theoretic fact (Schur multiplier / linearization obstruction for dihedral groups acting on P^1), with a slightly flawed but repairable argument. The motivating construction on the next page is part of known Teichmüller-tower themes.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'P(V_{P_n})(C) satisfait par les propriétés caractéristiques' – likely 'satisfait aux propriétés caractéristiques' (a crossed-out word precedes 'par'/'aux').
'comme analogue-droite-projective de [-...-] S_{P_n}': the struck symbol looks like an attempted 'P' (as in P^1 ⊃ S_{P_n}).
'qui se prolonge au quotient' is plausibly 'qui se restreint / se ramène' in sense; the handwriting suggests 'qui se ramène au quotient par ... m.Z'.
End of page: 'dans le cas [?] qui viennent en [?] ≡' should read '— ou, ce qui revient au même, qu'elle ne se remonte pas'.
'GP(V)' is Grothendieck's notation for the projective linear group PGL(V); 'Sl(V)' is the special linear group.
